ShortMeaning: Unique strategy name. Name lookup in Combo links and UseHookStrategy is case-insensitive.
Free-text note on the strategy (does not affect trading).
The strategy's detect algorithm (one of 23 types). When the type is changed in the editor, the fields of the other algorithms are kept in the profile in an inactive state.
Date and time the strategy was last saved (filled in automatically by the terminal).
Telegram only: name of the monitored Telegram channel. The special value MoonNews connects the Moon News system news feed (requires an active subscription on the kernel).

Telegram only: signal keyword (buy, moon_1..moon_20). For the MoonNews channel, a list of categories without # separated by commas or spaces (Listing, Delisting, etc.; an empty field accepts any news; MultiTokens=YES is recommended).

Telegram and UDP: allow text Trust Management commands (buy, sell, stop, short: and others). For Telegram, only from the ChannelName channel (and with the ChannelKey keyword, if set); for UDP, from signal packets.

UDP only: accept buy signals only from packets that passed the sender signature check; a plain (unsigned) packet is discarded. This verifies the source, not the secrecy of the content. The sell and sellAll commands for a coin are executed from plain packets too. Does not apply to the MoonCMD protocol. Enable only in a UDP strategy: in a Telegram strategy YES rejects all Trust Management commands.
When YES, suppresses automatic opening of the coin chart when the strategy signal fires.
Send a notification of the strategy detect itself to your Telegram channel (in a Kernel + Client setup the kernel does the sending).
Send reports on filled buys and sells of this strategy to your Telegram channel.
When the signal fires, play a sound alert and show a button for quick access to the coin chart.
Name of the predefined sound played when SoundAlert=YES.
How long the button with the signal coin's ticker stays above the chart, in seconds.
Index of a separate chart window (>= 0, 0 = off) to which the coin is added automatically after the strategy fires.
How long the coin chart stays in the AddToChart window, in seconds (0 = do not remove by timer).

Switches only this strategy to emulation: orders are filled inside the terminal, trades are marked (Emulator)/(E). Does not replace the Autotrading module (only the terminal's global emulation mode substitutes for it); virtual trades affect the coin's market session and pauses, virtual MoonShot orders count toward the shared order limit. In a kernel + client setup the detect runs on the kernel regardless of AutoBuy.

Write extended diagnostics of filter and detector rejection reasons to the logs/LOG_YYYY-MM-DD.log log (with 10 s anti-spam throttling per coin). The strategy editor highlights a forgotten flag with a warning, since it increases disk load.

Parameter of the Main tab. When NO, strategies of the same type are checked top to bottom; after the first match the rest are not checked on this signal. When YES, all strategies in a row give the signal up to the first one where the checkbox is cleared (chain): for several Drops to work in parallel, each needs the checkbox. Always on for NewListing, EMA, Spread, MoonHook, Activity; MoonShot, PumpsDetection, UDP, Combo, Manual, TopMarket, Alerts do not have the parameter.
Only when EmulatorMode=YES: do not write the strategy's virtual order operations to the logs/LOG_YYYY-MM-DD.log log (reset to NO automatically for real strategies).
Only when EmulatorMode=YES: do not keep the history of the strategy's canceled virtual Buy orders on the chart.
Use this strategy's own line style (OrderLineKind) and order colors (SellOrderColor, BuyOrderColor) on the chart.
Line style for the strategy's Buy, Sell and Trailing order lines on the chart when UseCustomColors=YES.
Color of the strategy's Sell order (take-profit) line in hexadecimal format when UseCustomColors=YES.
Color of the strategy's Buy order line in hexadecimal format when UseCustomColors=YES.
Whitelist of tickers separated by commas or spaces. The * mask is allowed only at the beginning (*PERP) or at the end (BTC*).
Blacklist of tickers separated by commas or spaces (* mask at the beginning/end). Not disabled by IgnoreFilters = YES.
Coin sorting metric for DynWL.
Sort DynWL in descending order (NO = ascending).
Number of coins (passing the filters and outside DynBL) for DynWL (0 = off). Not disabled by IgnoreFilters.
Coin sorting metric for DynBL.
Sort DynBL in descending order (NO = ascending).
Number of top coins of the selection for DynBL (0 = off). Built before DynWL; not disabled by IgnoreFilters.
DynWL/DynBL recalculation period in seconds (>= 5 s + 0..2 s jitter).

Skips all 6 subgroups (Base..Delta) (including CustomEMA for all strategies except SignalType = EMA, where the detector itself checks the formula). Does not disable: coin lists, Session, Triggers, OnlyNewListing, DontTradeListing, LeveragedTokens, ListedType, PreventWorkingUntil, SellByCustomEMA and the Quantitative rules.
Disables the Base filter subgroup entirely.
Disables the Time filter subgroup entirely.
Disables the Price filter subgroup entirely.
Disables the Ping filter subgroup entirely.
Disables the Volume filter subgroup entirely.
Disables the Delta filter subgroup entirely.
Continuously rechecks the filters while the Buy order is in place, canceling it when a value leaves the bounds (tolerance: deltas ±DeltaSwitch, ping +10%). Always on in MoonShot.
Disables the filter recheck immediately before the Buy order is sent (leaving only the check at detect).

Strategy pause before a repeat detect of the same coin: 1 + NextDetectPenalty s (0 = off). For Telegram, Combo, EMA, Spread, ChartWall, MoonHook and Activity it is disabled by IgnoreFilters = YES; for Watcher the pause is checked in the detect itself and is not disabled.
Shared pause per coin (s) for strategies with GlobalDetectPenalty > 0 after any detect. An active ChartWall keeps extending this pause on every order book tick.
Unix timestamp of the strategy pause (sgStop command). Checked before IgnoreFilters.

Formula (EMA, Avg, MAX, MIN, Vol, BTC, MAvg, Arb; AND/OR without grouping parentheses; windows 1s..300s, 2m..90m, 1h..48h; hourly data up to ~41h). Checked at detect and before buying; in MoonShot also while the order is in place. Collector thresholds (> -888, < 888, Vol > 0) skip the comparison but require data: a line made only of collectors is not checked before buying and writes the values to the report; a collector joined by AND drops coins without data. A syntax error blocks entries while Base filters are enabled. Requires the Autotrading module; disabled by IgnoreFilters/IgnoreBase = YES (for SignalType = EMA the detector checks the formula, but NextDetectPenalty and StrategyPenalty stop working).

Space-separated tags combined with AND (Monitoring, Fan, Seed, Launch, Gaming, New, BNB, Alpha, OICapped, TradFi; ! excludes: Fan !Monitoring). Requires the special tags API; Monitoring also works on Bybit and Gate.
Minimum leverage set in the terminal for the coin (>= 1).
Maximum leverage set in the terminal for the coin (0 = off).
Risk level (1..3) from @MoonInt at which the coin is blocked (4 = ignore; requires Telegram).

Risk level (1..3) from @MoonInt that stops the whole strategy: the strategy stops when the coin's level is at or above the threshold. The default 4 ignores the usual levels 1..3, but the AdminStop signal (level 10) still stops it; 0 stops the strategy at any level >= 1.

Lower threshold of the MarkPrice deviation from the futures price in % (> 0 = in the direction of the position, < 0 = against it; signs are inverted for Short). The value 0 turns the bound off (for zero, set -0.001). Disabled by IgnoreBase = YES.
Upper threshold of the MarkPrice deviation in % (1.0% protects against entering near liquidation; 0 = off). Disabled by IgnoreBase = YES.
Allows spot leveraged tokens (checked on Binance Spot before IgnoreFilters).
Cross-listing of the coin on Binance and Bybit: Ignore, Spot Only, Futures Only, Both. Checked before IgnoreFilters.
Work only during the first N s after the pair appears (0 = off). Checked before IgnoreFilters.
Do not trade the pair for the first N s after listing (0..345600 s, up to 4 days; only for listings noticed by a running terminal). Checked before IgnoreFilters.
Do not stop the strategy on Gate.io during the global order-limit penalty.
Pause of the strategy itself (s) on all coins after any time it fires; exists only for the EMA type (Base group). For the others, the shared pause across all markets is GlobalFilterPenalty.
Buy all tickers from one signal (recommended for MoonNews; otherwise only the first coin is taken).

Pause per coin (s) after 3 consecutive trades with an unfavorable exit price (average sell price worse than average buy price, fees excluded), a manual cancel or a click on the chart. In MoonShot it also raises the coin's priority if a profitable trade closed on it less than PenaltyTime s ago.
Pause per coin (s) after any trade whose exit price was worse than the entry price (by average prices, fees excluded; 0 = off).
Working schedule: HH:MM-HH:MM (interval within the day) or MM-MM without a colon (repeating minute interval 0..59 within every hour, e.g. 05-10 = from the 5th to the 10th minute of every hour).
Continuous weekly range (1 = Mon .. 7 = Sun, e.g. 1-5, 7.23:05-5.23:55, 1-5.21:00 = from the start of Monday to Friday 21:00; combined with WorkingTime by AND intersection).
Seconds before funding settlement (checked only on futures, skipped on spot): > 0 = work only during the last N s before funding; < 0 = pause for |N| s before funding (0 = off).
Seconds after funding settlement (checked only on futures, skipped on spot): > 0 = work only during the first N s after funding; < 0 = pause for the first |N| s after funding (0 = off).
Minimum coin price (0 = off).
Maximum coin price (0 = off).
Minimum order book price step in % (checked directly, without the DeltaSwitch extension).
Maximum order book price step in % (checked without DeltaSwitch; trap: the value 0 blocks all pairs).
Calculate PriceStepMin/Max from the corresponding BTC pair.
Limit on the total balance in all orders of the terminal, including the new OrderSize (0 = off).
Limit on the coin position in the terminal (active Buys + Sell remainders + OrderSize); with CheckAfterBuy = YES cancels resting Buy orders.
Do not open orders against an open position on the coin (MoonShot, Telegram, MoonHook).
Lower limit of the coin's total profit for the terminal session in $ (0 = off; Filters / Price tab, not Session).
Upper limit of the coin's total profit for the terminal session in $ (0 = off).

Filter by report result: while the total loss in the report for the interval set on the Autostart tab exceeds TotalLoss (a positive number in the report currency), the strategy does not enter new trades; not a kill switch: open trades, triggers and signals keep working, and entries resume when the result improves. Price group (bypassed by IgnorePrice/IgnoreFilters). 0 = off.
Upper ping limit in ms (0 = off). Trap: checked only when MaxLatency > 0. While an order is held (CheckAfterBuy) it is widened by +10%.
Lower ping limit in ms (0 = off; works independently of MaxLatency; while an order is held it is lowered by -10%).
Max. latency of the trade/order stream in ms (0 = off). When exceeded, sets a 7-second pause at the strategy level and enables the MaxPing check.

Threshold of the exchange-wide price lag in % (the largest lag among liquid pairs). When exceeded, the whole strategy, on all coins, is paused (90 s, longer on repeated peaks, up to 600 s). This is a kill switch for an exchange failure, not a coin filter.

Lower threshold of a specific coin's price lag in % (0 = off): take only coins whose lag is currently above the threshold, a spike radar. Do not combine with BinancePriceBug in one strategy: every Min rejection on a calm coin arms the same strategy pause as BinancePriceBug, and a strategy with both thresholds hardly trades.
Min. daily trading volume of the coin.
Max. daily trading volume of the coin (0 blocks the strategy).
Min. hourly trading volume of the coin.
Max. hourly trading volume of the coin (0 blocks the strategy).
Min. fast-updated hourly volume (0 = off).
Max. fast-updated hourly volume (0 = off).
Min. ratio of the minute volume to the reference average minute volume (1.0 = equal to the reference; 0 = off).
Max. ratio of the minute volume to the reference average minute volume (0 = off).
Enables the buy-to-sell volume ratio filter (BV/SV) over the BV_SV_TradesN window (Stops tab).
Minimum BV/SV ratio for entry.
Maximum BV/SV ratio (0 = off).
Min. coin price range over 3 h in % (>= 0).
Max. 3-hour delta of the coin in %. Actually checks Max(Delta_3h, Delta_1h).
Min. coin price range over 24 h in %.
Max. 24-hour delta of the coin in %. Actually checks Max(Delta_24h, Delta_1h).
First additional delta: 1h, 2h, 30m, 15m, 5m, 1m, Pump5m, Pump1h, Dump1h (all >= 0).
Lower bound of Delta2_Type in %.
Upper bound of Delta2_Type in %.
Second additional delta (1h, 2h, 30m, 15m, 5m, 1m, Pump5m, Pump1h, Dump1h).
Lower bound of Delta3_Type in %.
Upper bound of Delta3_Type in %.
Min. BTC change over 1 h in % (signed).
Max. BTC change over 1 h in %.
Min. BTC deviation from the 24 h average in %.
Max. BTC deviation from the 24 h average in %.
Min. BTC range over 5 min in % (>= 0).
Max. BTC range over 5 min in %.
Min. BTC range over 1 min in % (>= 0).
Max. BTC range over 1 min in %.
Min. average hourly delta of altcoins in % (signed).
Max. average hourly delta of altcoins in %.
Min. average 24-hour delta of altcoins in % (signed).
Max. average 24-hour delta of altcoins in %.
Market metric for the universal filter.
Lower bound of FilterBy (0 = off).
Upper bound of FilterBy (0 = off).
Pause for the whole strategy (s) when the BTC or market delta leaves its bounds (0 = off).
Delta hysteresis in % (min. 0.01%) with CheckAfterBuy = YES and in MoonShot: widens the corridor [X .. Y] to [X - DeltaSwitch .. Y + DeltaSwitch] after the order is placed.

Number of the key (1..202, 0 = off) activated when the master strategy's detect fires; for most detects also with AutoBuy = NO. Exceptions: MoonShot does not have this field (TriggerKeyBuy is activated by a buy and, with ActiveTrigger = YES, while the order is waiting); MoonStrike gives the detect key only with AutoBuy = YES and OrderSize > 0; the Manual strategy activates the key when a buy is placed and only with ActiveTrigger = YES. By default only on the signal coin (on all markets with TriggerAllMarkets = YES).

Number of the key (1..202) activated when the Buy order fills. Trap in MoonShot: with ActiveTrigger = YES the MoonShot strategy keeps TriggerKeyBuy active the whole time the limit Buy order sits in the order book, until the actual purchase.
Number of the key (1..202) activated after a trade closes with a positive profit (profit > 0, including a profitable close by SellByCustomEMA).

Number of the key (1..202) activated after a trade closes at a loss or at zero (profit <= 0). The same number in TriggerKeyProfit and TriggerKeyLoss gives a “trade closed” key regardless of the result.

Keeps the key (TriggerKeyBuy for MoonShot, TriggerKey for the others) active the whole time a buy is awaited: both while the real Buy order sits in the order book and while the strategy waits for the virtual BuyStop/BuyLimit to be crossed, so slaves are allowed in before the exchange order. After the buy fills or is canceled the extension stops and the slaves run out their TriggerSeconds. With ClearTriggersBelow/Above it clears the neighboring keys on every extension.
When YES, activates the trigger key globally on all trading pairs of the exchange at once; when NO, only on the coin where the master strategy fired.
When key $N$ is activated, clears all keys with strictly lower numbers ($1 \dots N - 1$). For example, with TriggerKey = 2 only key 1 is cleared. Used for step-by-step cascades.
When key N is activated, clears all keys with strictly higher numbers (N+1 .. 202), including the news keys 201 and 202.

Space-separated list of key numbers cleared when the strategy's own non-zero trigger fires (TriggerKey* > 0); with a zero event key the clearing is not invoked; applies to all strategy events. With TriggerAllMarkets = NO the strategy's own key in the list is cleared on this coin; with YES the global cycle activates it again. A non-numeric element is only written to the log.
Space-separated list of enabling keys (e.g. 1 5 12, or with individual lifetimes 1=300 5 7=900). By default works as OR (one active key is enough).
Switches the TriggerByKey check to logical AND: the slave strategy starts only when all keys listed in TriggerByKey are active on the coin at the same time.
Base lifetime (in seconds, up to 864000 s) for keys from TriggerByKey that have no individual timer set via key=time.

Space-separated list of blocking keys (trigger blacklist); supports the key=time format (1=300 5). While at least one of these keys is active on the coin, the strategy does not open new trades. Also serves as the mandatory external filter for SellByTriggerBL and CancelByTriggerBL.

Lifetime (s) of a blocking key from TriggerKeysBL written without its own =time. Default 0: such a key is not in effect for a single second: it does not block entry, does not cancel buys (CancelByTriggerBL), does not sell (SellByTriggerBL). Set the time in the list (102=120) or a non-zero TriggerSecondsBL.

Space-separated list of keys that close an open position. Numbers only: the entry 102=120 is an error here that forbids entries. The key must be listed in TriggerKeysBL and have a non-zero lifetime (102=120 there or TriggerSecondsBL > 0). The exit works like a sell on leaving the filters: via SellByFiltersDelay and Panic Sell at the strategy's stop.

Cancels resting Buy orders and conditional orders (BuyStop/BuyLimit) when any key from TriggerKeysBL is activated. Needed by strategies with CheckAfterBuy = NO: MoonShot and strategies with CheckAfterBuy = YES cancel buys on a blocking key without it. Does not cancel a filled buy.

Disables order blocking and scaling by the rules of the Session tab (sessions are off by default: YES). Does not reset the accumulated counter, only ignores the limits based on it; with YES the SessionResetTime decay does not work either.

Units of the SessionStratMax and SessionStratMin thresholds: YES = amount in the quote currency (USDT), NO = percentage of the base OrderSize (with OrderSize = 0 the base is $10, so with percentages set an explicit OrderSize).

Target profit threshold of one session (>= 0; strict comparison, zero does not turn the mechanism off: any profitable trade closes a positive session). When exceeded, the positive session counter is +1, the negative one is set to 0, the session result is reset, the strategy keeps working.
Percentage of linear increase of the SessionStratMax threshold with each next positive session, starting from SessionPlusCount (0 = threshold unchanged). Has no effect with SessionPlusCount = 0.

Loss limit of one session (a negative number, e.g. -100; strict comparison, with 0 any losing trade closes a negative session and starts the pause). When the result drops below the threshold, the negative session counter is +1, the positive one is set to 0, the result is reset, the strategy pauses for SessionPenaltyTime on this coin.

Percentage by which the allowed loss threshold SessionStratMin shrinks (a positive number) with each consecutive losing session, starting from SessionMinusCount. Has no effect with SessionMinusCount = 0.
Reset the accumulated positive profit of the current session after the very first losing trade if its loss exceeded |SessionStratMin| / 10.
Strategy pause time on the coin (in seconds) after a negative session closes by the SessionStratMin threshold.

Number of consecutive positive sessions from which the order size increase (SessionIncreaseOrder) and the profit threshold increase (SessionStratIncreaseMax) kick in. 0 (default) means the progression is off, not “from the first session”; for the order to grow right after the first positive session, set 1. Any negative session resets the positive session counter to 0.

Number of consecutive losing sessions from which the order size reduction (SessionReduceOrder) and the loss threshold shrinking (SessionStratReduceMin) kick in. 0 (default) means the reduction is off; for the order to shrink right after the first negative session, set 1. Any positive session resets the negative session counter to 0.

Percentage of exponential OrderSize increase on each positive session starting from SessionPlusCount (0 = off; has no effect with SessionPlusCount = 0 either; the actual change is logged as OrderSize increased by ...).

Maximum addition to the order in % of the original OrderSize (ceiling OrderSize * (100 + SessionIncreaseOrderMax) / 100; the value 500% means growth by at most 6 times, +500% over the base; allowed range 0 .. 5000%).

Positive percentage of OrderSize reduction for each losing session starting from the SessionMinusCount-th: the order is divided by (1 + SessionReduceOrder/100) for each next negative session (20: 1000 → 833 → 694). 0 = off; has no effect with SessionMinusCount = 0 either. A negative value is reset to zero on save, no reduction.

Division limit in %: the order will not become smaller than OrderSize / (1 + SessionReduceOrderMin/100); default 500 = not less than 1/6 of the base. Range 0..5000; negative values are reset to zero (reduction turns off).

Session decay period in seconds (0 = off): every SessionResetTime seconds, on all coins of the strategy the session result is reduced by 10% and the non-zero positive and negative session counters are decremented by 1. Works only with IgnoreSession = NO.

Allows automatic placement of a Buy order when the detect fires. With NO the strategy only gives a signal (alert, trigger, mark on the chart), an aid for manual trading. In a kernel + client setup the detect of the checked strategies runs on the kernel regardless of AutoBuy.

On futures, opens a short position. On spot, sells a token already on the balance without borrowed funds (with OrderSize = 0, the whole remainder); auto-borrowing on Binance margin is a separate terminal setting (MoonBonus).
Order size in the quote currency (0 = take the order size from the global settings on the terminal's main screen).

Type of the opening order: Buy = a real limit order in the order book; BuyStop (above the price, breakout) and BuyLimit (below, sell-off) = pending levels in the terminal's memory which, once crossed by both the order book and the average trade price, place a real limit order for 3 seconds regardless of AutoCancelBuy. No reversal check.

Offset in % of the real order from the BuyStop/BuyLimit pending order level after it is triggered: the order is placed deeper into the market to fill with higher probability; the sign sets the side. Fill is not guaranteed.
Buy price offset in % from the base market price at the moment of the signal (negative = below the market, positive = above).
Treat buyPrice as the exact absolute coin price rather than a percentage offset. Works only in the NewListing strategy.
Measure buyPrice from the last trade price (with NO the base is the current best ASK price).
Measure buyPrice from the minimum ASK price over the last 30 seconds instead of the current price.
Measure buyPrice from the price as of N seconds ago (0 = use the current price).
Pause before sending the Buy order after the detect, in milliseconds (0..3000 ms). Lets you skip the first tick of the impulse.

Auto-cancel timer for an unfilled Buy order in seconds (fractional values supported; 0 = do not cancel). In MoonShot forced to at least 15 s; in the other strategies moving the order restarts the timer. Note: the default 300 s also cancels the conditional orders BuyStop/BuyLimit after 5 minutes.
Auto-cancel timer for the Buy order (s) in Telegram strategies when the buy was placed at the lower price from the signal text (TlgBuyDipPrice).
Cancels the remaining Buy orders on the coin right after a Sell order of the same strategy fills (or an order with the same non-zero JoinSellKey).
Maximum number of simultaneously active orders (Buy and Sell) of this strategy (0 = no limit). In MoonStrike strategies the limit is counted in total across all strike strategies of the terminal.
Maximum number of simultaneous orders of this strategy on one coin (0 = no limit).
Maximum number of different coins on which the strategy can hold orders at the same time (0 = no limit; not applied to MoonStrike).
Strict single-order-per-market mode: forbids entry if the coin already has an active trade, disables the grid (OrdersCount = 1) and JoinSellKey merging.
Sends the Buy order with the exchange PostOnly flag (maker only): if the order crosses the spread and would fill as a taker, the exchange rejects it automatically.

Request validity window recvWindow in milliseconds for opening Buy orders (and on Bybit WS API also for selling and Amend modification; 0 = standard window). With a network delay above HFT ms the exchange rejects the late order without an API rate-limit penalty. The window is counted from a timestamp the terminal itself aligns with the exchange clock; an HFT rejection is a normal event on a ping spike (chapter 07).
Check before the signal fires that the free balance is enough to place the whole OrdersCount grid.
Minimum free balance in the quote currency below which the strategy does not place new orders (0 = off).
For Telegram strategies: if the signal text contains stop-words about buying on a pullback, use the TlgBuyDipPrice price instead of the regular buyPrice.
Buy price offset in % from the market when TlgUseBuyDipWords = YES fires.
Trust Management (TM) protection: the maximum allowed excess of the buy price over the current market price in %, above which the external command is ignored.
Number of grid orders per signal. In the Free version limited by the global setting for the maximum number of grid orders. In MoonShot, UDP and with OneOrderPerMarket = YES forced to 1.

Price step between grid levels in %. A negative step lays the grid against the position in both long and short (in a long the legs are below, in a short above the first order; the terminal mirrors the direction itself, no need to change the sign). A positive step goes with the position (breakout); in a short the legs are below the first price and may fill immediately on a drop. Step normalization protects the last order's price from reaching zero.
Law for the distance between price levels in the grid: Linear (even step in % of the first price) or Exponential (multiplier (1 + BuyPriceStep * (k - 1) / 100)^k of Price1 for the k-th order).
Step of the grid order size change in %. For all orders to have the same size, set 0 with OrderSizeKind = Linear and 100 with OrderSizeKind = Exponential.
Law for the grid order sizes: Linear adds OrderSizeStep % of the first order at each step; Exponential multiplies the previous order's size by |OrderSizeStep| / 100.
Lifetime increment (in seconds) for each next grid order on top of the base AutoCancelBuy. Has no effect with AutoCancelBuy = 0.

Disables the auto-cancel timer (AutoCancelBuy) for all remaining waiting Buy orders of the grid as soon as the first order in sequence fills (including a partial fill with cancellation of the unfilled remainder). Lets you hold a deep averaging grid until the position closes.
Manual trading only (Manual) with OrdersCount = 1: automatically splits a large Buy order into parts when it exceeds the exchange limit for the maximum order size.

Number of the Sell order auto-merge group (0 = auto-merge off; for manual orders the global merge settings apply). Joins real Sell orders of one coin and direction with the same key into a common exit, inheriting the sell and stop-loss parameters from the first running strategy in the list with this JoinSellKey (or, if none is running, from the first checked one). Not applied in Spread strategies and with OneOrderPerMarket = YES.

Price of the merged take-profit: YES = the positive calculated SellPrice percentage of the owner strategy from the new average entry price (not applied to MoonHook and MoonStrike, which use the common path); NO = the arithmetic mean of the current percentages of the merged Sell orders (not weighted by size) from the same entry price, with a possible market adjustment. The money target and the first order's percentage are not kept.
Weight of the coin's 3-hour delta in the SumDelta total.
Weight of the coin's hourly delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the coin's 15-minute delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the coin's 5-minute delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the coin's 1-minute delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the coin's daily (24h) delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the whole market's hourly delta (taken as an absolute value, always >= 0) in SumDelta.
Weight of the whole market's 24-hour delta (taken as an absolute value, always >= 0) in SumDelta.
Weight of the BTC hourly delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the BTC 5-minute delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the BTC 1-minute delta in SumDelta.
Weight of the mark price (MarkPrice) deviation in SumDelta.
Weight of the current per-coin PriceBug price lag (including Latency) in SumDelta. Lets you push the buy deeper during exchange lags (MoonShot uses its own MShotAddPriceBug parameter).
Weight of the hourly rise Pump1h (from the price an hour ago to the hour's maximum) in SumDelta.
Weight of the hourly drop Dump1h (from the price an hour ago to the hour's minimum) in SumDelta.
Upper limit of the total modifier adjustment (0 = no limit). The absolute value of the sum is used; there is no lower limit.

Multiplier for adding SumDelta to the detect threshold (Threshold + SumDelta * DetectModifier). Trap in MoonHook: raises the lower threshold HookDetectDepth but does not shift the upper ceiling HookDetectDepthMax; once the upper limit is exceeded the detect stops firing.
Multiplier for adding SumDelta to the buy price (buyPrice + SumDelta * BuyModifier; a negative value places the order lower in a volatile market).
Multiplier for adding SumDelta to the take-profit price (SellPrice + SumDelta * SellModifier).

Multiplier of the modifier adjustment to the main stop level: a positive value moves the stop farther from the entry, a negative one tightens it. The actual shift is in the log as StopLoss adjusted [...].

Automatically place a Sell order after the buy. On futures forced on (YES); turning it off (NO = leave the coins on the balance) is available only on spot (the tooltip mentions ExpertMode; the current code has no such check).

Target take-profit price in % of the actual buy price (adjusted by this strategy's SellModifier, Delta Modifiers tab; in MoonShot/MoonHook/MoonStrike/Spread it may be overridden by the profile sell levels).
Only for NewListing with SellFromAsset = YES: SellPrice is the absolute sell price of the asset already held, not a percentage. Has no effect on a regular NewListing entry.
Pause before placing the Sell order after the buy (0..3000 ms), so as not to show the take-profit volume in the first moments of the impulse.
Share of the order volume (0..50%) split off into a separate order by the Split Piece context menu command, the SellPiece panel or the SellPiece Telegram command.
If SellPrice is not above 1%, may raise the take-profit (up to 2%) by placing the order below a large sell wall.
NewListing only: at the listing start, do not buy but immediately sell the asset already on the spot balance at the SellPrice price.
NewListing only with SellFromAsset=YES: quantity of coins to sell (0 = sell the whole available asset balance).
Timer in seconds from the moment the Sell order is placed (0 = off), after which the position is closed when the market leaves the bounds of the strategy filters (does not check CustomEMA).

Two-phase exit when SellByFilters fires: at >= 0.1 s, first moves the limit Sell order once to the current price (but not below PriceDownAllowedDrop), and after SellByFiltersDelay s turns on Panic Sell.

Exit condition formula: when true (after SellEMADelay) the position is closed as on a filter exit: with SellByFiltersDelay the take-profit is first moved to the market, then Panic Sell at the strategy's stop. Works with IgnoreFilters=YES; requires the Autotrading module. The collector threshold > -888 with SellEMACheckEnter=YES forbids buying wherever the formula has data; with NO it closes the position right after entry. To disable, leave the field empty (0 is an error that blocks entries). After the close, arms TriggerKeyProfit/Loss.
Delay in seconds from the moment the Sell order is placed before the SellByCustomEMA check starts.

Check the SellByCustomEMA formula before entry: if it is already true at the moment of the signal, the buy is blocked (even with IgnoreFilters=YES); otherwise the position would close right after the buy.

Exchange conditional stop order in the supported mode: only the Manual strategy (and remote control orders), Binance, the SM button. With a negative MarketStopLevel the closing order is placed on the exchange immediately as a stop at that level; the stop and the take-profit are not in place at the same time: an order in the direction of the position is a take-profit, against it a stop (below the price for a long, above for a short). The order type and execution depend on the exchange. Has no effect in automatic strategies.

Initial level of the exchange stop order in % of the entry price (negative) with UseMarketStop = YES in the Manual strategy. 0 sets no initial stop but does not forbid converting the closing order into an exchange stop manually.

Time in seconds from the placement of the Sell order to the first take-profit lowering step (0 = algorithm off). SellLevel moves do not reset the countdown; when take-profit orders are joined by JoinSellKey a new take-profit is created and the countdown starts over.
Interval in seconds between subsequent Sell order price lowering steps.
Size of one Sell order price lowering step in %.

Base for the PriceDownPercent step: with NO an absolute percentage of the current order price is subtracted; with YES, a share of the remaining distance between the current Sell and the buy price (with PriceDownToAllowedDrop=NO the order approaches the entry price asymptotically without going below it).

With PriceDownRelative=YES, calculate the step not from the distance to the buy price but from the distance between the current Sell and the PriceDownAllowedDrop threshold (lets the order be lowered smoothly into the red with a negative PriceDownAllowedDrop).

Lower limit (in % of the buy price) down to which PriceDown (and also the first phase of SellByFiltersDelay) may lower the Sell order. Trap on Short: at values <= -100 the calculated price goes negative and blocks the lowering; set a reasonable limit (e.g. -20).
Delay in seconds from the buy to the first move by SellLevel (0 = algorithm off). If SellLevelDelayNext = 0, also sets the interval between repeated moves.
Interval in seconds between the second and subsequent moves of the Sell order by the SellLevel algorithm.
Depth of the trade history window in seconds in which the maximum for the sell level calculation is searched (0 = off); by default an hour, including the time before the entry.

Adjustment to the found maximum in %: with SellLevelRelative=NO it is added to the maximum (the default +0.2 places the take-profit above the maximum, a negative value below it); with YES, a share of the distance from the entry price to the maximum.
If YES, places the take-profit at SellLevelAdjust % of the difference between MaxPrice over SellLevelTime and the buy price (BuyPrice + (MaxPrice - BuyPrice) * Adjust / 100).
Maximum number of take-profit moves by SellLevel. Does not affect the PriceDown timer: both algorithms run at the same time.

SellLevel working time in seconds after the buy: 0 = no limit, otherwise must be greater than SellLevelDelay (the value 1 effectively turns the algorithm off). A manual take-profit move does not turn SellLevel off (it stops only PriceDown).
SellLevel move condition (in % of the buy price): if the calculated level is lower, the move is postponed until a better maximum.
Flag that disables the SellShot algorithm: to activate the tracking, set IgnoreSellShot = NO.
Delay before SellShot turns on, from the moment the Sell order is placed, in seconds (fractional values supported, >= 0).

Base take-profit distance in % above the “market”, the price maximum over SellShotCalcInterval s (the minimum in a short). SellShot overrides the base take-profit (SellPrice, HookSellLevel, the MoonStrike level) within SellShotAllowedDown..Up. A tiny distance = a take-profit at the ask edge; a negative distance and AllowedUp = immediate close.

Width of the SellShot working corridor in % of SellShotDistance (1..99), ±SellShotCorridor % of the distance each way: with a distance of 1% and a corridor of 50 the take-profit is held between 0.5% and 1.5% of the price and moved when it leaves the bounds.
Window in seconds (0.1 .. 25.0 s) for calculating the market price extreme (maximum for Long, minimum for Short) from which SellShotDistance is measured.
Pause in seconds (>= 0) before moving the take-profit farther from the market (up in a Long) when the price rises.
Pause in seconds (>= 0) before moving the take-profit closer to the market (down in a Long) when the price pulls back.

Distance shrink rate, %/s, set with a minus sign (-0.05 = the take-profit moves 0.05% closer to the price every second): Dist(T) = SellShotDistance - |SellShotPriceDown| * (T - SellShotDelay - SellShotPriceDownDelay). A positive value is replaced by zero on save, no shrinking.

Additional delay in seconds before the distance starts shrinking by SellShotPriceDown: counted after SellShotDelay, so shrinking starts SellShotDelay + SellShotPriceDownDelay seconds after the Sell order is placed.
Upper ceiling (in % of the buy price) above which SellShot does not raise the take-profit.
Lower floor (in % of the buy price) below which SellShot does not lower the take-profit.
Flag that disables the SellSpread algorithm: to activate, set IgnoreSellSpread = NO.
Minimum current spread in % (>= 0) at which SellSpread moves the take-profit.
SellSpread start delay in seconds from the moment the Sell order is placed (fractional values supported).

Take-profit offset inward from the far edge of the spread in % of the spread width (with a 5% spread and -10% the take-profit is placed at 4.5% from the bottom of the spread). Automatically clamped to [-100 .. -1] (a positive number becomes -1).
Lower limit (in % of the buy price) below which SellSpread does not lower the Sell order.
Maximum number of take-profit moves by the SellSpread algorithm (0 = no repeated moves).
Telegram strategies only: take the stop-loss levels from the signal text (if the signal has no stop, the strategy settings apply).

Enable the main stop loss. A disabled stop creates no fallback floor: the depth of an exit by filters, formula or the Panic Sell button is set by the strategy's AllowedDrop. Stop moving (SecondStopLoss, StopLoss3) and pulling the stop toward liquidation require UseStopLoss = YES.
Do not recalculate the absolute stop-loss price when orders are merged (JoinSellKey) or the grid fills (the first order's stop level is kept).

Faster stop check by trade and order book prices without waiting for the smoothed average: exit earlier on a sharp breakout. Does not guarantee triggering on the first single spike or a fixed reaction time. Not recommended in MoonShot.

On any Panic Sell of this order (stop, trailing, BV/SV stop, exit by filters, formula or key, delisting, manual button) close with a market order instead of the limit cascade. Supported on Binance, Bybit, Gate and Bitget (spot and futures); not applied to a short on spot and on the other exchanges. If the exchange did not fill the market order, a limit order at the current price is attempted and the regular Panic Sell by StopLossSpread/AllowedDrop follows; closing is not guaranteed.

Price smoothing for the stop-loss check (0 = off; modes 3, 5, 10) so that a single spike does not knock out the stop. Works in the long check with FastStopLoss = NO; the current short path has no similar ASK smoothing. Smoothing does not guarantee the result.

Activation delay for StopLoss 1/2/3 and Trailing in seconds (fractional values supported) from the moment the Sell order is placed. The Stop 2/Stop 3 switch timers count in parallel with StopLossDelay.
Main stop-loss level in % of the buy price (set with a minus sign; adjusted by this strategy's StopLossModifier, Delta Modifiers tab).

Initial offset of the Panic Sell closing order (in %, 0.1 .. 10) from the lowest of the current prices, the best bid and the latest trades (mirrored in a short); the offset grows with each move. The site recommends 0.4 .. 1.5.
Coefficient widening StopLossSpread by the coin's minute volatility: adds the coin's minute delta multiplied by StopSpreadAdd1mDelta (PriceBug not involved).

Limit (% of the entry price) down to which the Panic Sell closing limit order may chase the price after a stop or an exit by filters/formula; this is not a loss level. The actual floor is another StopLossSpread lower. < -98 (default -99) = no floor. Too tight a limit may prevent closing on a squeeze. UseMarketOrder ignores it.

Isolated margin only with leverage > 1: forbids Panic Sell from placing the closing order worse than the calculated liquidation price (log: Stop level (...) is below than liq level). In the emulator and backtest the protection may hold the virtual exit; turn it off for tests. The UseMarketOrder market order ignores the protection.

Offset (%) from the exchange liquidation price, two uses: pulls the main stop toward liquidation (requires UseStopLoss = YES) and limits take-profit lowering by the PriceDown algorithm (independently of the stop). 0 = not applied.
Automatically close the open position by stop when a coin delisting notification arrives from the @MoonInt system channel (requires consent to statistics exchange to be enabled).
Enable the second stop loss (StopLoss 2), activated when TimeToSwitch2Stop and PriceToSwitch2Stop are both met.
Time in seconds from the moment the Sell order is placed, after which switching to SecondStopLoss is allowed.

Price threshold (in % of the buy price) for enabling the second stop: the price must be on the favorable side: for a long the best Bid above the “entry + threshold” level, for a short below the mirrored level; TimeToSwitch2Stop must also have elapsed and the stop loss must be enabled. For the stop to switch in the loss zone too, set a negative value (e.g. -10).
New stop-loss level (in % of the buy price) after StopLoss 2 is activated. Moves the main stop: does not work without UseStopLoss = YES; the chase floor after the second stop is the main AllowedDrop.
Enable the third stop loss (StopLoss 3), activated when TimeToSwitchStop3 and PriceToSwitchStop3 are both met.
Time in seconds from the moment the Sell order is placed until switching to StopLoss3 is allowed.
Price threshold (in % of the buy price) for switching to StopLoss3: the price must be on the favorable side: for a long above the “entry + threshold” level, for a short below the mirrored level.
Third stop-loss level (in % of the buy price).

Chase limit of the closing order (in % of the buy price, >= -99) after the third stop triggers (the second uses the main AllowedDrop). If after triggering the price fell below the starting stop, the deeper of the two limits is allowed.
Enable position tracking with a trailing stop.

Pullback distance from the peak price in % at which the trailing close triggers (converted to a negative sign). Triggering starts Panic Sell with the TrailingSpread spread; the global “Add … to trailing per each % of price” slider changes the trailing of strategy orders too.
Spread of the Panic Sell closing order in % (0.1 .. 5.0) when the trailing or the BV/SV stop triggers; a value <= 0 is normalized to 0.1 when the strategy loads.
Number of ticks (0 = off) for smoothing the PeakPrice peak price, so that a single upward spike does not lift the trailing line into an empty ASK order book.

Allow the trailing to trigger only while the price is above the TakeProfit level (by the average trade price and by the last trade), and on triggering raise the chase floor to the TakeProfit level (StopLossSpread below it). Meaningless without trailing.
Base protected profit level in % of the buy price for activating the trailing with UseTakeProfit=YES.

Closing the position by the ratio of flows in the trade feed over BV_SV_TradesN trades or seconds (BV_SV_Kind): for a long, buys to sells; for a short, sells to buys; exit when it falls below BV_SV_Ratio. The stop is active while the smoothed bid and the last trade are above the BV_SV_TakeProfit threshold (below in a short; the threshold may be negative, default -1); once the price returns past the threshold the stop is inactive. With BV_SV_TakeProfit < 0.1 the threshold also works as an entry filter.
Unit of the BV/SV ratio calculation window: 'TradesCount' (over the last N trades) or 'Time' (over the last N seconds).
Size of the BV/SV calculation window: number of trades or seconds depending on BV_SV_Kind.
Threshold BV/SV ratio for the stop exit (and for entry pre-filtering with BV_SV_TakeProfit < 0.1).

Price threshold of the BV/SV stop in % of the entry (default -1): the stop works while the price is on the favorable side of the threshold (at -1, also in a small loss; at +1, only while the price is above +1%). At a value < 0.1 the BV_SV_Ratio threshold additionally serves as an entry filter.

Swaps the numerator and denominator of the BV/SV stop fraction (for a long, sells to buys); exit when this fraction falls below the same BV_SV_Ratio, i.e. when the flow goes your way. The threshold is set as the reciprocal (exit a long when buys are twice the sells: BV_SV_Ratio = 0.5). Does not affect the entry filter.

MoonShot fast mode (on by default): with a non-zero MShotRaiseWait the “current” price is the deepest trade of the last instant rather than the last one in the batch, and the take-profit is placed immediately on the fill. Also applies to MoonHook (there the “current” price is chosen this way with HookRaiseWait > 0). Slow down the moves via MShotReplaceDelay, not by clearing the checkbox; against the take-profit closing in the same spike, a small SellDelay.
Near edge of the corridor in % of the current price (>= 0.001%): when the price comes closer than this threshold, the order is moved back to MShotPrice.

Distance from the reference price at which the order sits (in %; below for a long, above for a short). The far edge of the corridor is built automatically: MShotPrice + min(MShotPriceMin, MShotPrice − MShotPriceMin); with 3/2 the corridor is 2…4%, with the default 7/2 it is 2…9%. If MShotPriceMin > MShotPrice, on save MShotPrice is raised to MShotPriceMin + 0.001 and the corridor degenerates into a line.
Do not place the limit order right at the MShotUsePrice reference price: for coins with a coarse price grid (step ≥ 1%) an order without an offset effectively sits at the market.
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's 3-hour delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's hourly delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's 15-minute delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's 5-minute delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's 1-minute delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the 5-second price range (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the coin's 24-hour delta (0 .. 1).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the whole market's hourly delta (0 .. 10).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the BTC hourly delta (0 .. 10).
Corridor adjustment coefficient per 1% of the absolute BTC 5-minute delta (0 .. 10).
Adjustment coefficient from the price divergence from MarkPrice (applied only when the MarkPrice deviation points in the order's direction).

Adjustment coefficient per 1% of the minute cross-exchange price spread (0 .. 1). The spread is never less than the coin's minute delta, and without arbitrage price sources it equals it; then the parameter works like MShotAdd1minDelta.
Coefficient for pushing the order away during exchange lags in proportion to the PriceBug metric (0 .. 5; the total contribution is capped at 30%).

Percentage of additional widening of the corridor width itself from the sum of deltas: the order (and the far edge with it) is shifted by AddDelta * (1 + MShotAddDistance / 100), which lowers the move frequency and saves API limits in high volatility.

After the buy the take-profit is placed at the higher of two prices: the strategy's SellPrice and the ask minus MShotSellPriceAdjust; the ask is the higher of two: before the spike (a few seconds before the hit) and the current one. The point is to sell on the return to the price the coin was knocked down from; SellPrice works as the lower bound. NO = a fixed take-profit in percent.
Adjustment in % (0 .. 20%) subtracted from the ask (the higher of the pre-spike and the current one) when calculating the take-profit with MShotSellAtLastPrice=YES.

Pause (s) before moving the order deeper when the price has come closer than MShotPriceMin. A trade-off: with zero the order manages to escape from under a fast spike; with a delay the spike fills the limit order, but a slow slide fills it more often too. The tooltip names values around 0.032–0.064 s for shots on a series of hits. The price returning into the corridor resets the countdown.

Pause (s, default 30) before pulling the order toward a price that moved away: protection against a counter-move after a surge; at the same time the window in which the price minimum (maximum in a short) for measuring MShotPrice is searched: minutes in this parameter glue the order to a long-passed bottom. Any move resets the countdown.

Coin ranking metric for selecting markets to work (Last1mDelta..24h-Delta, Pump5m/1h, Dump1h, DailyVol/HourlyVol/MinuteVol, DVolToHVolAsc/Desc, MaxOrder, Orders, Session, MaxPos, MarkPrice, Funding, Leverage, OrderBook).
MShotSortBy sort direction: YES = descending, NO = ascending.

Reference price of the order: Trade (recommended) = the worse of the latest trade price and the best bid (ask in a short), the order book when the feed is stale; BID and ASK look only at the order book and do not see trades through it. ASK is written in capitals, Trade in any case; any other spelling is read as BID.

Repeat shot on the same coin while the position is still open: checked in the MShotRepeatDelay..MShotRepeatWait window after the take-profit is placed, by the conditions MShotRepeatIfProfit (above the entry) and MShotRepeatIfDrop (below, averaging). The averaging branch is always on: with the defaults 0/0 a repeat is placed on almost any price deviation from the entry; to repeat only after a rise, set MShotRepeatIfDrop deliberately deep. Requires the Autotrading module or the global emulator; the repeat takes the coin out of turn and is not counted in MaxActiveOrders. This is a repeat entry, not an exit.
Repeat shot condition on a rise: the current price must be above the entry price by more than the specified % (0 = at any price above the entry).

Repeat shot condition for averaging on a drop (<= 0): the price must go below the entry price by the specified % (0 = at any price below the entry). The branch cannot be turned off: a positive value becomes 0 on save. To avoid averaging, set a depth the price will not reach within the repeat window.
Upper edge of the window in seconds from the take-profit placement within which the repeat shot condition is checked.

Lower edge of the window in seconds from the take-profit placement from which the MShotRepeatIfProfit/MShotRepeatIfDrop conditions start being checked (with MShotRepeatDelay >= MShotRepeatWait the check window is empty).

Spike search window in seconds (clamped to 0.4 .. 10.0 s): the spike, the pullback and the HookRollBackWait wait must fit into it. Also sets the repeat-detect pause on the coin (about HookTimeFrame plus a second, separately for long and short) and the turnover evaluation window for BuyOrderReduce.
Minimum spike depth in % over the HookTimeFrame window (increased by this strategy's DetectModifier).
Maximum allowed spike depth in % (0 = no upper limit; not shifted by DetectModifier).
Minimum total trade volume in USDT within the HookTimeFrame window (0 = not checked; filters out empty spikes on illiquid coins).

Count the spike only if for several windows before it the price held above the bottom by at least the detect depth (by the windows' low prices): a return to the previous level after a short upward surge does not count as a spike.
Required percentage of the price pullback from the spike bottom relative to its depth (>= 0%), confirming that the “hook” has formed.
Upper limit of the pullback in % of the spike depth (0 = no limit).
Time the price must hold above the HookPriceRollBack level, in milliseconds (100 ms cuts off a single tick; the whole event including the wait must fit into HookTimeFrame).
How much the coin had already fallen over the ~30 seconds before the spike, in % of the spike's own depth (200 = the preceding drop is twice the spike); lower bound, 0 = no condition.
Ceiling of the preceding drop in % of the spike depth (see HookDropMin); 0 = no limit.
Direction of the tracked spikes: 'OnlyLong', 'OnlyShort' or 'Both'.

Invert the entry direction relative to the spike (e.g. open a Short on a downward spike). The first order then sits on the other side of the price; with HookPriceDistance > 0, in the middle of the hook corridor: in modes 0/1 that is one spike depth from the price, the HookInitialPrice level is not used.

What the first order (HookInitialPrice) is measured from: 0 = from the bottom upward by a fraction of the spike depth; 1 = from the pullback price downward by the same fraction (0 = a whole depth below the pullback); in 0/1 with HookPriceDistance > 0 the first order also stays inside the hook corridor (see HookInitialPrice); 2 = like 0, but the corridor is fitted to the order, and with HookPriceDistance > 0 the signal is skipped if the level is not below the current price (so HookInitialPrice sets the minimum pullback); 3 = from the current price downward on the inverse scale by (100 − HookInitialPrice)% of the depth; 4 = the same, but as a fraction of the pullback. In 3/4 the smaller the number, the deeper the order.

Level of the first Buy order placement in % (-500 .. 200); what it is measured from is set by HookInterpolate: with 0 and 2, from the spike bottom upward by a fraction of the depth; with 1, from the pullback price downward by the same fraction; with 3 and 4, on the inverse scale from the current price by (100 − HookInitialPrice)% of the spike depth (3) or the pullback height (4): 100 = right at the price, 0 = a whole depth / the whole pullback, negative = deeper. In modes 0/1 with HookPriceDistance > 0 (default 25) the first order stays inside the corridor: no closer than (100 − HookPriceDistance)% and no farther than (100 + HookPriceDistance)% of the spike depth from the current price (spike 110 → 100, pullback 105, mode 0, HookInitialPrice = 25, HookPriceDistance = 25: about 97.8 instead of 102.5). The order sits exactly at HookInitialPrice only with HookPriceDistance = 0 or a wide corridor.

Width of the order tracking corridor: in modes 0/1, in % of the spike depth (after a move the order sits at one depth from the price: spike 5%, 10 → corridor 4.5…5.5%), and this corridor already limits the first placement (see HookInitialPrice); in modes 3/4, in % of the “order – price” distance; in mode 2 the corridor is fitted to the order, roughly from half to one and a half “order – price” distances, but not deeper than (100 + HookPriceDistance)% of the spike depth: here the parameter only limits the corridor and enables tracking; for manual hooks, in % of the click depth. 0 = the order does not move. A manual hook does not work without a width.

Hook take-profit as a fraction of the spike depth: with HookSellFixed = NO it is measured from the distance between the calculated entry price and the spike top (100 = sell at the top if the entry went at the calculated price); with YES, HookSellLevel % of the depth is added to the actual entry price regardless of where the fill happened.
When YES, always adds the fixed amount HookSellLevel * Depth to the actual buy price, regardless of the level inside the spike at which the Buy filled.
Delay in seconds (>= 0) before moving the Buy order deeper on a new impulse against the position.
Pause (s, default 30) before pulling the order closer to the price; at the same time the extreme search window: the initial 30 seconds keep the order under the old bottom.
Cancel delay for a partially filled Buy order in milliseconds (0 = the remainder is canceled immediately).

Re-arm threshold with HookRepeatAfterSell = YES: the closed trade's profit must be strictly greater (0 = any positive; zero and losing trades give no repeat). With a grid, a single order is placed again.
Automatically place a repeat MoonHook order after the take-profit closes (subject to HookRepeatIfProfit).

In the Manual strategy (Strategy settings tab): name of the slave MoonHook that tracks the manual order in the corridor, sets the take-profit from the click depth and re-arms the hook. On save the slave is switched to slave mode: AutoBuy is enabled, OrderSize is zeroed, the run checkbox is cleared.

Breakout depth of the reference bid line in % with the MStrikeAdd* distance adjustments; on save not less than 0.1% on spot and 0.01% on futures. Without AutoBuy = YES and OrderSize > 0 there is no MoonStrike detect at all.

Money volume of market sells (buys in a short) at the moment of the strike in the quote currency; on save not less than 0.01 on spot and 1 on futures (there the default 0.2 becomes 1). The default is a legacy of BTC pairs; on USDT pairs set a real amount.
Reserved smoothing parameter (not used in the calculation in current versions).
Futures only: spike hunting direction ('OnlyLong', 'OnlyShort' or 'Both').
Addition in % to the MStrikeDepth threshold per 1% of the coin's hourly delta (<= 1).
Addition in % to the MStrikeDepth threshold per 1% of the coin's 15-minute delta (<= 1).
Addition in % to the MStrikeDepth threshold per 1% of the market's hourly delta (<= 20).
Addition in % to the MStrikeDepth threshold per 1% of the BTC hourly delta (<= 10).
Pause before sending the Buy order (0 .. 3000 ms), during which the terminal keeps measuring the downward extension of the spike.

Buy order level in %: with MStrikeBuyRelative=YES, from the spike bottom upward as a fraction of the depth (0 = at the bottom, 50 = at the middle); with NO, with a minus sign from the price before the spike started (-5 = 5% lower). In NO mode zero and positive values put the order at the spike start level, effectively a market buy.
MStrikeBuyLevel reference mode: YES = in % of the recorded spike depth from its bottom; NO = in absolute % of the pre-spike price.

Wait (up to 9 s) for the first trade priced higher than the previous one (lower in a short) before sending the Buy order: a sign that the extreme has stopped updating, not a confirmed reversal. No such trade within 9 s = the entry is canceled with the record Strike waited too much; this is normal.
Take-profit level in % of the spike depth, measured from the spike's lowest point.
When YES, measures the take-profit from the minimum of three prices (spike bottom, calculated entry price and actual buy price); useful on short 1..3% spikes.
Length of the trade feed analysis window in seconds (0.5 .. 30.0 s).

Minimum share of time within TimeInterval during which trades at different prices were going on (%), i.e. how continuous the feed is. Trap: on save clamped to 10 .. 100 (0 does not turn the filter off but becomes 10%).

Minimum feed continuity before the detect window (0 .. 100%): filters out coins that were just lying flat; to catch the start of a pump from the bottom, set 0. With TimeInterval longer than ~15 s the check reaches inside the window itself and loses its meaning.
Minimum number of trades in each short slice of the detect window where there were trades (0 = off): filters out a feed of rare single prints.
How many equal slices (1 .. 100) to divide TimeInterval into to check the minimum PriceSpread on each of them; with more than five slices one is allowed to miss the threshold.
Number of additional checks of the window shifted back by fractions of a second (0 .. 5): requires the spread conditions to hold on all shifted windows to filter out single spikes.

Minimum price range (>= 0.01%) on each of the PriceIntervals slices of the window (with more than five slices one is allowed to miss the threshold); the range of the whole window is at least three price steps.
Maximum allowed total price range over the whole TimeInterval window in % (0 = no upper limit).
How many of the last PriceIntervals slices to use for calculating the spread bounds when placing the order (0 = calculate over the whole TimeInterval).
Position of the base buy price inside the found spread in % (for Long measured from the bottom of the spread upward, for Short from the top downward; the general buyPrice is applied on top of it).
Target sell level inside the spread in % of its width: the resulting take-profit is the farther one in the trade direction of SellPrice and this level.

Window in milliseconds for estimating the allowed volume by the average feed turnover: estimate = detect window turnover × BuyOrderReduce / window length in ms (in Spread the window is TimeInterval, in MoonHook HookTimeFrame).

Minimum threshold of the calculated volume in USDT with BuyOrderReduce > 0: if the feed turnover estimate gives a volume below the threshold, there is no detect (Spread logs Reduced order would be too small, MoonHook skips the signal). In both strategies the order itself is reduced to the estimated volume (not below the exchange minimum); a manual hook is not reduced.
Look for the spread in a horizontal price corridor without a pronounced trend.
Window in milliseconds (0 .. 30000 ms, 0 = off) for calculating the buy-to-sell volume ratio filter (BV/SV for Long, SV/BV for Short).
Upper limit of the BV/SV ratio over the Spread_BV_SV_Time window (0 = off).
Lower limit of the BV/SV ratio over the Spread_BV_SV_Time window (0 = off).
Lower bound of the spread direction vector (-100 .. +100, calculated over the last 5 seconds of the window).
Upper bound of the direction vector (-100 .. +100): the sign is tied to the chart and is not flipped for a short; “only downward spikes” is SpreadPolarityMax = 0.

Repeat entry in the first seconds after the sell is placed if the price has moved toward the take-profit by more than the given % of the distance; the repeat is also placed when a profitable sell filled within those same first seconds (0 .. 100, 0 = off; at 100 only the repeat after a profitable sell remains; no more than five repeats; requires the Autotrading module).
Drop analysis window in seconds (<= 2000); zero blocks the detect.
Smoothing of past prices in seconds (< 2 = no averaging). Keep it small (0..2): with a large value the past peak is counted weakened, and triggering needs a noticeably deeper sell-off than set.
Number of 2-second ticks for averaging the final (lower) price of the sell-off (0 = no averaging, reacts to fast spikes).
Required drop depth in % over DropsMaxTime (increased by DetectModifier). Zero does not turn the detect off but keeps it from firing; fill in both DropsPriceDelta and DropsMaxTime.
Require that the current price at the moment of the detect also sets a new hourly low of the coin.
Measure buyPrice from the final (lower) price of the sell-off, averaged over DropsLastPriceMA, instead of the current order book price.
Time in seconds during which the price in front of the wall must hold within the narrow WallsPriceDelta corridor.
Maximum allowed scatter of the 5-minute candle lows over WallsMaxTime in %; the price sits on a shelf. Strict comparison: zero (the default) does not turn the detect off but blocks it.
Search depth for supporting demand in the order book in %, down from the lower shadow of the shelf, not from the current price.
Threshold of the total demand in the BID order book, from the best price down to the WallBuyVolDeep depth under the shelf, in the quote currency; the sum must be greater than the threshold.
The same total demand (see WallBuyVolume) must be greater than this % of the coin's daily trading volume.
Ceiling of the total supply in the ASK order book (up to the WallSellVolDeep height) in % of the found demand. Strict comparison: zero (the default) does not turn the detect off but blocks it.
Height of the ASK order book scan in %, up from the upper edge of the shelf (the highest of the candle lows), not from the current price; the supply up to this height is compared by WallSellVolToBuy.
ChartWall: threshold of the total order book volume (in the quote currency) in the WallSpread band from the best price; the detect fires when the volume is greater than the threshold.
ChartWall: width of the order book band from the best price in % within which the volume is summed.
ChartWall: which side of the order book to sum: YES = ASK, NO = BID. The trade direction is set separately by the Short parameter, not by the order book side.
Window for measuring the price rise impulse in PumpsDetection: '4s', '15s', '30s' or '60s'.

Price rise over PumpPriceInterval, in %, from the lowest bid price in the window rather than from the price at its start, must be greater than the threshold (the threshold is increased by DetectModifier). In the terminal only the topmost enabled PumpsDetection strategy works.

Number of buys over the PumpVolEMA window (not shorter than two seconds) must be greater than the threshold: with the defaults, more than fifteen buys in two seconds, not in one (the tooltip says “per second”).
Buy volume over the same window must be greater than the threshold (in the market's quote currency).
Exponential smoothing window for the per-second buy volume in seconds (>= 1 s).

How many seconds after the take-profit is placed (0 = off) to pull the take-profit once toward the pump peak by PumpMovePersent. The countdown starts from the take-profit placement, not from the detect as the PumpMovePersent tooltip says.

Offset from the peak in % of the “entry → peak” path: after PumpMoveTimer s the take-profit is moved once to the level entry + (peak - entry) × (1 - PumpMovePersent/100), not below breakeven. 50 = the middle, the default 0.5 = almost at the peak. If the pump did not reach the take-profit, the take-profit is lowered to the peak (earlier exit).
Measure the buy price from the price 2 seconds ago (unless Use30SecOldASK is on), protecting against entering at the very top of the tick.
Volumes: length of the short (signal) window in seconds (4 .. VolLongInterval div 2).
Volumes: minimum price range (maximum to minimum, without direction) over the short interval in %; strict comparison: zero does not turn the condition off, the range must still be greater than zero.
Volumes: length of the long (background) window in seconds (120 .. 3600 s).
Volumes: how many times the buy volume (BV) in the short window must exceed the average per-minute background volume in the long window, excluding the short window.
Volumes: minimum ratio of the normalized long-window volume to the coin's hourly volume.
Volumes: maximum ratio of the normalized long-window volume to the coin's hourly volume.
Volumes: minimum ratio of the normalized long-window volume to the coin's daily volume.
Volumes: maximum ratio of the normalized long-window volume to the coin's daily volume.
Volumes: minimum buy-to-sell volume ratio (BV/SV) in the short interval.
Volumes: minimum absolute buy volume (BV) in the short interval in the quote currency.
Volumes: maximum allowed sell volume (SV) in the long interval excluding the short window, in the quote currency.
Volumes: use the maximum price of the long interval (protects against a false signal on a bounce from the bottom).
Volumes: minimum total demand in the BID order book above the minimum price of the short interval.
Volumes: minimum total demand in the BID order book above the maximum price of the short interval (of the long one with VolTakeLongMaxP = YES).

Volumes: required growth of the total demand above the short-interval maximum during the order book confirmation (several re-reads) before the order is placed; no growth = no signal. No more than 15 coins are in confirmation at once; extra signals are dropped silently.
Volumes: required growth of the total demand above the short-interval minimum over the same time.
Volumes: BID order book scan depth in % of the current ASK price.
Volumes: minimum total BID order book volume at the volBidsDeep depth.
Volumes: ASK order book scan height in % of the current ASK price.
Volumes: minimum ratio of the BID sum (at the volBidsDeep depth) to the ASK sum (at the volAsksDeep height).
VolumesLite: length of the base window T0, the oldest, calm stretch before the acceleration, in seconds.
VolumesLite: length of window T1, the first acceleration stretch after the T0 base, in seconds.
VolumesLite: length of window T2, the second acceleration stretch, in seconds.
VolumesLite: length of the most recent window T3, which ends at the last trade, in seconds.
VolumesLite: minimum rise of the average price from the T0 base to the next window T1 in %.
VolumesLite: minimum rise of the average price from T1 to T2 in %.
VolumesLite: minimum rise of the average price from T2 to the recent T3 in %.
VolumesLite: maximum allowed price rise on each of the transitions P1..P3 in %.

VolumesLite: by how many percent the price growth rate of the second transition (P2) exceeds the first (P1), relative acceleration, strict comparison: rates of 1% and 1.5% give 50, not 0.5; at 0 the second rate simply must be higher than the first.
VolumesLite: the same for the third transition (P3) against the second (P2).
VolumesLite: maximum allowed price range (Max - Min) inside the base window T0 in % (“the coin was calm before the acceleration”).
VolumesLite: maximum allowed excess of the peak price over the interval's average price in % (filters out single spikes).
VolumesLite: minimum volume growth from the T0 base to window T1 in %.
VolumesLite: minimum volume growth from T1 to T2 in %.
VolumesLite: minimum volume growth from T2 to the recent T3 in %.
VolumesLite: method for calculating the average prices on the intervals (YES = volume-weighted average VWAP, NO = average by trade count).
VolumesLite: with YES compares per-minute volumes, with NO the full volume sums over the interval.
Waves: length of the base window T0, the oldest stretch before the waves, in seconds.
Waves: length of wave window T1, the first after the T0 base, in seconds.
Waves: length of wave window T2, the second after the base, in seconds.
Waves: length of the most recent wave window T3, which ends at the last trade, in seconds.
Waves: change of the average price from the T0 base to window T1 in % (> 0 = rise of at least, < 0 = drop of at least, 0 = do not check).
Waves: change of the average price from T1 to T2 in % (> 0 = rise, < 0 = pullback/drop, 0 = do not check).
Waves: change of the average price from T2 to the recent T3 in % (> 0 = rise, < 0 = drop, 0 = do not check).
Waves: price range in the base window T0 in % (> 0 = range above the threshold, < 0 = flat with range below |WavesDelta0|%, 0 = off).
Waves: maximum deviation of the price peak from the interval's average price in % (spike filter).
Waves: volume change from the T0 base to window T1 in % (> 0 = volume growth, < 0 = volume decline, 0 = off).
Waves: volume change from T1 to T2 in % (> 0 = growth, < 0 = decline, 0 = off).
Waves: volume change from T2 to the recent T3 in % (> 0 = growth, < 0 = decline, 0 = off).
Waves: calculate the volume-weighted average price (YES) or the simple average over trades (NO).
Waves: with YES normalizes the interval volumes to one minute, with NO takes the full interval volume.
Delta: long interval for analyzing price and volume changes, in seconds.
Delta: short interval for averaging the price and measuring the current impulse, in seconds.

Delta: minimum price range over two DeltaInterval intervals in %, between the maximum and minimum of prices averaged over DeltaShortInterval slices; up or down, the direction is set by DeltaLastPrice; the threshold is raised by DetectModifier.
Delta: minimum total volume (BV + SV) over DeltaInterval in the quote currency.
Delta: minimum volume growth in the current DeltaInterval compared with the previous interval of the same length, in %.
Delta: minimum weighted per-second volume before the detect (0 = off).
Delta: deviation of the average price of the last short interval from the average price of the long interval in % (> 0 = rise, < 0 = drop, 0 = off).
Liquidations: liquidation cascade counting window in seconds.
Liquidations: minimum number of liquidations in the LiqTime window (0 = do not check).
Liquidations: minimum total liquidation volume over LiqTime in USDT; strict comparison: zero still requires a non-zero volume.
Liquidations: maximum total liquidation volume over LiqTime in USDT (0 = no upper limit).
Liquidations: minimum quiet pause after the last liquidation in milliseconds before entry (0 = off).
Liquidations: maximum time in milliseconds since the last liquidation during which the signal stays valid (0 = off).

Liquidations: filter by window direction. All liquidations of the LiqTime window count toward LiqCount and the volume, and the window's direction is the side whose liquidations are larger by volume: 'Both' = any window, 'OnlyLong' = only with long liquidations prevailing, 'OnlyShort' = short liquidations, 'Combo' = two consecutive detects with opposite direction, 'Twice' = two consecutive with the same (at least NextDetectPenalty between detects).

Liquidations: YES (default) = open a position in the same direction as the liquidated positions (after long liquidations on a sell-off, a long to buy back); NO = against them, along the cascade. A “long liquidation” = a forcibly closed long, i.e. a sell.
Liquidations: window in milliseconds for calculating the BV/SV entry filter (0 = filter off).

Liquidations: the ratio of the feed volume against the cascade to the volume along it over Liq_BV_SV_Time (after long liquidations, buys to sells; after short liquidations, the reverse) must be greater than the threshold. The default 0.5 does not yet mean the counter-flow prevails; prevalence starts at a threshold above 1; with the ratio below the threshold the terminal waits for it to recover.
Combo: name of the first (starting) strategy of the link (case-insensitive lookup). MoonShot and MoonStrike cannot be combo members; a member with AutoBuy = NO does not show its own signal.
Combo: name of the second (final) strategy of the link.
Combo: minimum time interval in seconds between the ComboStart and ComboEnd triggers.
Combo: maximum time interval in seconds between the ComboStart and ComboEnd triggers.
Activity: analysis window for the concentration of equal market-maker trade sizes in seconds (15 .. 60 s).
Activity: lower bound of the size of the MM orders being searched for, in USD (>= 100, <= MMOrderMax - 10).
Activity: upper bound of the size of the MM orders being searched for, in USD (120 .. 200000).
Activity: width of the bin by which trade sizes are grouped, in USD (1 .. (MMOrderMax - MMOrderMin) div 10).
TopMarket: minimum 15-minute range (Last15mDelta) of the market-leading coin in % (among coins that passed PriceStepMax; a repeat signal is given only after the leader changes).
TopMarket: enter in the direction of the leader's smoothed price deviation from the hourly average (YES: above the average = long, below = short) or against it (NO).
Alerts: check the crossing of the user's alert line by actual trades (YES) or by the smoothed average price (NO).

List of tracked Hyperliquid addresses (0x...) separated by spaces or commas, the strategy's address book. Applied when the strategy is saved and on Start; the coin is determined from the address's trade itself, no open chart is needed.
Which wallet operations to react to: 'Both' (any trades), 'OnlyOpen' (only opening/building a position), 'OnlyClose' (only closing).

Entry direction relative to the tracked address's position (not its last trade): YES = toward its position, NO = against it. With WatchDirection = OnlyClose this is not copying the exit: when a whale closes a long, with YES the terminal opens a long.

Pulling the order price toward the address's trade price, in % (0 = off): before exchange rounding, choose the higher of the calculated price and the watched fill multiplied by (1 + WatchPriceDeviation / 100) for a long, or the lower of the calculated price and the fill divided by that factor for a short. Does not cap the price: it keeps the limit order from lagging behind a market that has moved away after the whale.
Minimum total volume of a batch of the tracked address's trades on the coin in USD (>= 0).

Minimum address position in USD: the address's original position on the coin (before the fill) plus the added volume of the trade or batch is compared, i.e. |position before the trade| + volume, not the remainder after it (closing 9,000 out of 10,000 gives 19,000); within a batch the check may run per individual fill. Filters out small addresses; does not distinguish a partial close from a full one.
